history.summary: Historic temple dedicated to Lord Panduranga (Vithal, an incarnation of Vishnu/Krishna) at Chilakalapudi, a suburb of the port town Machilipatnam in Krishna district. Per the Government of Andhra Pradesh (Krishna district tourism page), it was constructed in 1929 by Sri Bhakta Narasimham on a six-acre campus; the deity and garbhagriha closely resemble the Pandharpur Vithoba temple, and separate shrines house Radha, Rukmini and Satyabhama with an Abhayanjaneya Swami idol in front of the main sanctum. The sanctum is entered from the west with the deity facing east, and devotees of all communities are allowed to touch the deity's feet. LEGEND FLAG: a devotional blog claims the idol is swayambhu (self-manifested) and calls this the second most revered Panduranga shrine after Pandharpur - these are devotional claims, not in official sources; the official record says built 1929. CSV STATE FLAG: the CSV state field says 'Machilipatnam', which is a city, not a state; the correct state is Andhra Pradesh. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Machilipatnam' is imprecise - the temple is at Chilakalapudi, ~4-5 km from Machilipatnam town. DISTRICT NOTE: using 'Krishna' per the official AP government tourism page; newer sources may say Machilipatnam district (carved from Krishna in 2022).

name: Panduranga Swamy Temple (Chilakalapudi)
town_description: Chilakalapudi is a suburb of Machilipatnam in Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh, near Manginapudi beach. It is best known for the 1929 Panduranga Swamy temple modelled on the Pandharpur Vithoba temple.

travel.railway: Machilipatnam station (~4 km per holyshrines); Chilakalapudi station ~1 km (per indianetzone - verify)
travel.road: Machilipatnam bus stand ~5 km (per holyshrines); local buses and autos available
